items.title: 6.3.4 Tangents and Normals to a Parabola (Condition of the tangency to Parabola) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 186-187: 6.3.4 tangent via dy/dx, normal, condition of tangency c = a/m for y^2 = 4ax.

blocks.text: Tangent (woh line jo curve ko sirf ek jagah halka sa chhoo kar guzar jaye) aur normal (us chhone wale point par tangent ke perpendicular line) hum circle ke liye 6.2 mein dekh chuke hain. Ab parabola ki baari hai.

Parabola ke kisi point par tangent ki equation nikalne ke liye pehle parabola ki equation se \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) nikal kar us point par tangent ki slope maloom karte hain. Phir line ki point-slope form se tangent ki equation likh lete hain.
Kyun ke kisi point par curve ka normal usi point par tangent ke perpendicular hota hai, is liye normal ki equation tangent ki equation se foran mil jati hai.
Lekin kitab yahan pehle ek aur dilchasp sawal uthati hai: koi line kab parabola ko sirf chhooti hai?

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan do purane khayal ek saath istemal hote hain.
Kisi point par tangent ki slope = us point par \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) ki value (differentiation, Unit 2). Yaani derivative curve ki 'dhalaan' batata hai.
Perpendicular lines: \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\), is liye normal ki slope \(= -\frac{1}{\text{tangent ki slope}}\) (Unit 5).
Yeh rule har curve par lagta hai; 6.3.5 mein ise \(y^{2} = 4ax\) par lagayenge. Neeche kitab pehle ek doosra sawal hal karti hai: koi di gayi line parabola ko kab chhooti hai?

Ek line ki equation lijiye
\[y = mx + c\ \text{...(1)}\]
aur parabola
\[y^{2} = 4ax\ \text{...(2)}\]
In ke milne ke points nikalne ke liye (1) aur (2) ko ek saath hal karte hain. (1) se \(y\) ki value (2) mein rakhne par:

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab teesri line \(m^{2}x^{2} + 2mcx - 4ax + c^{2} = 4ax\) chhapti hai. \(4ax\) ko baayen le jaane ke baad daayen taraf 0 bachta hai: \(m^{2}x^{2} + 2mcx - 4ax + c^{2} = 0\). Hum ne upar sahi line likhi hai. Agli line (3) kitab mein sahi hai.
Line (1) parabola (2) ko tab chhooti hai (tangent hoti hai) jab (3) ke roots barabar hon. Is ka matlab hai ke (3) ka discriminant D zero hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab likhti hai: "Line (1) is tangent to (3) if roofs of (3) are equal." Sahi yeh hai: line (1) parabola (2) ki tangent hai jab (3) ke roots barabar hon. (3) to quadratic equation hai, curve nahi; aur 'roofs' darasal 'roots' hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Barabar roots ka matlab tangent kyun? (3) ka har root line aur parabola ka ek common point deta hai.
\(D > 0\): do alag roots, do common points; line curve ko kaat kar guzarti hai (secant).
\(D = 0\): ek hi root do baar, dono points mil kar ek ho gaye; line sirf chhooti hai, yaani tangent.
\(D < 0\): koi real root nahi; line curve se milti hi nahi.
Socho ek seedhi chhari ko pyale ke kinare par rakhte hain: agar woh andar dhans jaye to do jagah lagti hai, agar bilkul kinare ko chhoo kar ruke to ek jagah. (Yeh tab hai jab \(m \ne 0\). Horizontal line \(y = c\) parabola se sirf ek point par milti hai magar use kaat kar guzarti hai; woh kabhi tangent nahi.)

Ab hum isi discriminant wali shart ko algebra se khol kar dekhte hain. Har line ke saath sochte jaiye ke kaun sa term kahan se aaya. Pehli line mein seedha \(B^{2} - 4AC = 0\) likha hai; doosri mein bracket ka square kiya; phir 4 se divide kiya taake numbers chhote hon; phir \((mc - 2a)^{2}\) ko khola aur dekha ke \(m^{2}c^{2}\) dono taraf se cancel ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yahan quadratic (3) ko \(Ax^{2} + Bx + C = 0\) samjhein: \(A = m^{2}\), \(B = 2(mc - 2a)\), \(C = c^{2}\), aur \(D = B^{2} - 4AC\). \(m^{2}c^{2}\) dono taraf se cancel ho jata hai, yahi is derivation ki khoobsurti hai. Phir \(4amc = 4a^{2}\) ko \(4a\) se divide kiya (ijazat hai kyun ke \(a \ne 0\)) aur \(mc = a\) mila.
Is tarah line \(y = mx + c\) ke parabola \(y^{2} = 4ax\) ki tangent hone ki shart \(c = \frac{a}{m}\) hai.

Natija: kisi bhi non-zero real number \(m\) ke liye line \(y = mx + \frac{a}{m}\) parabola \(y^{2} = 4ax\) ki tangent hai. Isi tarah doosre parabolas ke liye bhi tangency ki shart nikali ja sakti hai.

Is natije ko ghaur se dekhiye: slope \(m\) aap jo chahein rakh lein (zero ke ilawa), har slope ke liye bilkul ek tangent hai aur us ka \(y\)-intercept \(\frac{a}{m}\) hai. Yaani parabola ki har direction mein ek hi 'chhone wali' line hoti hai. Yeh baat Exercise 6.3 ke Q10 mein seedhi kaam aayegi, jahan tangent ek di gayi line ke parallel chahiye: parallel ka matlab same slope, aur phir \(c = \frac{a}{m}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Point of contact (chhone ka point; hamari taraf se izafa, Exercise 6.3 Q10 mein kaam aayega). \(c = \frac{a}{m}\) ho to (3) ka dohra root
\[x = -\dfrac{B}{2A} = \dfrac{2a - mc}{m^{2}} = \dfrac{a}{m^{2}}\]
aur phir \(y = mx + c = \frac{a}{m} + \frac{a}{m} = \frac{2a}{m}\). Yaani line point \(\left(\frac{a}{m^{2}}, \frac{2a}{m}\right)\) par chhooti hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
\(y^{2} = 8x\) ki woh tangent nikaliye jis ki slope 2 ho.
Yahan \(4a = 8\), yaani \(a = 2\); \(m = 2\) se \(c = \frac{a}{m} = 1\). Tangent: \(y = 2x + 1\).
Tasdeeq: \((2x + 1)^{2} = 8x\) se \(4x^{2} - 4x + 1 = 0\), yaani \((2x - 1)^{2} = 0\): dohra root \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), point of contact \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, 2\right)\), jo \(\left(\frac{a}{m^{2}}, \frac{2a}{m}\right)\) se bhi yahi aata hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya line \(y = x + 3\) parabola \(y^{2} = 12x\) ko chhooti hai? (\(a = 3\), \(m = 1\), \(\frac{a}{m} = 3 = c\). Haan! Point of contact \((3, 6)\).) Aur \(y = x + 2\)? (\(c = 2 \ne 3\); yeh curve ko do points par kaatti hai.)

Poore section ka khulasa ek kahani mein: line ki equation parabola mein daali, ek quadratic bani; quadratic ke roots common points hain; tangent ka matlab ek hi common point, yaani barabar roots, yaani discriminant zero; aur is shart ko simplify kiya to \(c = \frac{a}{m}\) nikla. Yahi chaar qadam (substitute, quadratic, \(D = 0\), simplify) ellipse aur hyperbola mein bhi isi tarah lagenge, sirf algebra thori lambi hogi.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Kisi point par tangent: us point par \(\frac{dy}{dx}\) = slope, phir point-slope form.
2. Normal: tangent ke perpendicular, slope \(= -\frac{1}{\text{tangent ki slope}}\).
3. Line ko conic mein substitute karne se quadratic banti hai; barabar roots (\(D = 0\)) ka matlab line chhooti hai.
4. \(y = mx + c\) parabola \(y^{2} = 4ax\) ko sirf tab chhooti hai jab \(c = \frac{a}{m}\) (\(m \ne 0\)); point of contact \(\left(\frac{a}{m^{2}}, \frac{2a}{m}\right)\).

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \((mx + c)^{2}\) ko \(m^{2}x^{2} + c^{2}\) likh kar \(2mcx\) bhool jana.
2. \(B = 2(mc - 2a) = 2mc - 4a\) ki jagah \(2mc - 2a\) le lena.
3. Doosre parabolas ke liye bhi \(c = \frac{a}{m}\) laga dena. Yeh sirf \(y^{2} = 4ax\) ke liye hai; doosre parabola ke liye substitution dobara karein (6.3.5 dekhiye).
4. \(m = 0\) par \(D = 0\) lagana: horizontal line \(y^{2} = 4ax\) ki kabhi tangent nahi hoti.
